body: SOCOM II U.S. Navy SEALs is Zipper Interactive's PlayStation 2 tactical shooter, first released in North America on 4 November 2003. The sequel continues the combination of a command-led single-player campaign and online team competition. Twelve offline missions take the squad to Albania, Algeria, Brazil and Russia, giving each part of the campaign another setting and set of objectives. The player remains responsible for more than the next shot. Keeping the operation under control means deciding how the team should approach the area and what each order should accomplish.

The campaign offers several ranks, with the harder settings unlocked by completing earlier requirements. Returning to a mission gives the player another chance to understand its approaches and use the squad more effectively. Objectives also unlock material such as music, concept art and multiplayer character models, providing smaller rewards beyond finishing the story. The tactical structure makes familiarity useful: knowing an enemy's position can change when the group moves and which route becomes safe. A better attempt begins before the first exchange, through a more informed plan for the team.

Online competition became a major part of SOCOM II's identity, using voice communication to turn separate players into an organised team. David Sears returned as director, while Inon Zur composed the score. The European release followed in March 2004. The official servers closed in August 2012 together with other original SOCOM releases. Its importance belongs partly to the habits formed around it: arranging a match, recognising familiar teammates and using spoken information to make a shared decision. Those routines helped define what online console play could become during the PlayStation 2 years.
